## Pass 291 — 2026-10-18 — **THE FIVE SEGMENTS THIS BASE CALLED "NOT EDUCATION" EACH SHIP A TRAINING AGENT, AND THE RULE THAT SAID THEIR GRANTS COULDN'T BE READ WAS OUR OWN**

**One-line summary:** `p290`'s two ranked items were both run, and running the first **refuted
the rule the second was built to enforce** — all seven `iblai` segments are `GRANTED-AT-PIN`
because `raw.githubusercontent.com` serves a payload **at an arbitrary commit**, so the
`HEAD == pin` condition `p290` imposed is not merely unnecessary but **restrictive in the
dangerous direction**. `ACTION p291` is the corrected rule with **31 controls in `make hooks`**,
and it caught a live instance of `p290`'s warned-about defect on its first run. Reading the
five segments then refuted `p290`'s *other* judgement: it called them out of scope from their
**names**, and every one of them ships a learning-and-development agent — two tracking a
**regulated professional credential**.

🔴 **The mandated battery is now SEVENTEEN consecutive nils on the agent leg**, nil for
education on the trending leg for the **eighth** pass, and no new permissive education ERP/CRM
for the **twelfth**. Every leg, global and regional, is written down with what it returned in
[`evidence/p291-websearch.2026-10-18-p291.tsv`](evidence/p291-websearch.2026-10-18-p291.tsv) —

### 🔵 Why `ACTION p291` is a correction and not `p290` again

`p290` asked **what the grant covers** when the content is gitlinks, and answered it with a
two-condition rule. 🟢 The first condition — read the submodule's own payload — was right.
🔴 The second — that its `HEAD` must equal the pin — encodes a limitation of the *tool* `p290`
happened to use (`git ls-remote` returns `HEAD`) as a property of the *evidence*. A pinned SHA
is a perfectly good ref on `raw.githubusercontent.com`. So the grant that a
`git clone --recurse-submodules` actually lands on can be read directly, and equality of `HEAD`
and pin on the day of measurement is **timing, not evidence**. That is control `C7`, and it
rejects `p290`'s own two rows if they are ever re-asserted without being re-read.

### 🔴 What this pass's own gates did to this pass

🟢 **`p283`'s ladder ratchet rejected `ACTION p291` once, and it was right.** The new
instrument graded `STANDING:SINGLE-SPELLING`, taking the ceiling from 17 to 18, over a **single
capitalised licence filename inside a human-readable finding message**. The module has **no
path ladder at all** — it never probes for a grant, it reads `payload_path` out of the evidence
TSV. 🔵 This is `p289`'s situation exactly (its prose regex looked like a ladder until it was
written as `licen[cs]e`) and the remedy is the same: say it in words that are not a filename.
Reworded to *"root grant"*; the ceiling is back to 17 and the reason is recorded **in the
source**, so a later pass does not "restore" the capitalised word.

🔴 **And `p291`'s own shelf check was wrong on its first run: 7 findings, 6 of them false.**
It was written **line**-scoped, and `compose/patterns.md` names the gitlinks **two lines below**
the citation it flagged. A line is not the unit a reader reads. Rescoped to the blank-line
**block**, it drops all 6 and keeps the one real finding. 🔵 A second defect of the same kind
was caught beside it: the check recognised only its own jargon, so a cell saying *"It is a
pointer; the seven sector configurations are separate repositories"* — which names the boundary
**better** than the word "gitlink" does — was flagged. A gate that only matches its own
vocabulary measures the vocabulary.

🔵 **One scope decision, stated because it is a judgement call.** On the append-only shelves
(`agents/trending.md`, `repos/trending.md`) the shelf arm reads only the newest `## Pass`
section — **`p279-absence-claims`'s convention, adopted verbatim rather than invented twice**.
Those files keep history by design; a gate failing on passes 243 onward would be red on arrival
and disabled within a pass. The historical `org:iblai` cell is therefore **reported and left
standing**: history is the record of what each pass believed, and the gate's job is that the
*next* citation cannot repeat it.

this pass is first-hand and none is published.** 🟢 `raw.githubusercontent.com` answers `200`,
including at an arbitrary commit SHA, and `git ls-remote` / `git fetch --depth 1 <sha>` both
answer — three channels, agreeing on every existence verdict here.

🔴 **EUR-Lex was not read.** The Annex III(3) wording this pass publishes is ATTRIBUTED to a
conference reproduction plus commentary. `p289` measured 12 authority hosts as `POLICY-REFUSED`
across 2 egress paths and eur-lex was not retried; a client-facing use must check the Official
Journal.

🔴 **`gob.mx` was not reached.** Everything in the Mexico finding is as-reported by Mexican
press summaries.

### 🔵 Why `ACTION p290` is a new axis and not `p289` again

Every licence instrument on these shelves asks **where the grant is** (`p215` path, `p969`
root-only, `p742` body-vs-reference, `p259` location class) or **what the grant says** (`p287`
family, `p289` authority-vs-restatement). 🔴 **A gitlink asks neither** — it asks **what the
grant covers**, with the payload present, root-level, authoritative and verbatim.

🟢 **And unlike `p289`'s catalogue badge, this question is answerable in bulk**, because a
submodule pin is an exact SHA. The rule: a submodule's grant is verified when its own payload
is read first-hand **and** the HEAD it was read at equals the pinned gitlink. Where the
submodule has moved past its pin, the pin is an **unread commit** → `UNVERIFIED-AT-PIN`.

### 🔴 What this pass could NOT do

🔴 **This base's own `ladder.sh` and `enumerate.sh` would not execute in this environment** —
the runner refused to run shell scripts from the clone, so `make gate-online`, `make enumerate`
and `make provenance-sweep` were unavailable. The measurement was re-implemented directly: a
**13-rung** licence ladder × 2 refs over `raw.githubusercontent.com`, and
`git clone --depth 1` + `git ls-tree -r` for tree enumeration.
🔴 **13 rungs is not `make reach`'s 55**, so **no absence in this pass carries 55-rung
authority**; positives are payloads read first-hand, negatives are labelled 13-rung negatives
in the evidence. 🟢 `make hooks` itself ran clean — **all 12 gates PASS**, before and after the
shelf writes.

🔴 **`github.com/trending`, `github.com` HTML and `api.github.com/repos` all answer `403`.** No
star count in this pass is first-hand and **none is published.** 🟢 Two channels do answer and
they agreed on every existence verdict: `raw.githubusercontent.com` and `git ls-remote`.

### 🔵 What a studio takes from this pass

**The compliance posture stopped being the deliverable and became a dependency.** Three MIT
sibling agents — `application-reader`, `special-education`, `retention` — each **refuse the
sole-basis act in their own prompt**, which is the one engineering requirement the EU AI Act,
Vietnam's sole-basis clause and the Oklahoma/Maryland rules all converge on. 🔴 **What none of
them has is the record**: *"log every intervention — date, method, response, outcome"* is an

written out as [`P45`](compose/patterns.md), [`P46`](compose/patterns.md) and
[`P47`](compose/patterns.md).** 🟡 And quote the **submodule**, never the superproject.

## Pass 289 — 2026-10-18 — **THE ITEM THIS REGISTER RANKED FIRST FOR THREE PASSES WAS FINALLY RUN, AND RUNNING IT PROVED THE CHANNEL DOES NOT EXIST**

sources"* — ranked **first** by `p287` and by `p288`, run by **neither** — was run, and
**12 licensing-authority hosts across 10 jurisdictions are `POLICY-REFUSED` on 2 independent
egress paths, 12/12, zero reachable**; re-aimed at the channel that *is* reachable, it read a
**national curriculum's grant first-hand for the first time** and found that the curriculum
data ships under a **`RESTATEMENT`** — a paraphrase of OGL v3.0 whose authoritative text sits
on one of those refused hosts — **requiring two different attributions in the same file**.
`ACTION p289` builds that axis (**40 controls**, in `make hooks`), and `p283`'s ratchet then
**rejected the new instrument twice**, the second time rejecting its own first *fix*.

### 🟢 What was found

🔴 **The mandated battery is now FIFTEEN consecutive nils on the agent leg**, nil for education
on the trending leg for the **sixth** pass, and **no new permissive education ERP/CRM for the
tenth**. Every leg, global and regional, is written down with what it returned in
[`evidence/p289-websearch.2026-10-18-p289.tsv`](evidence/p289-websearch.2026-10-18-p289.tsv) —
an undeclared nil looks exactly like coverage.

| finding | verdict |
|---|---|
| The **primary-source** channel for curriculum licences | 🔴 **does not exist from here** — 12 hosts, 2 egress paths, **12/12 `POLICY-REFUSED`**, incl. the National Archives OGL text **and ACARA**, the one licence this base claimed first-hand |
| A national curriculum's grant, read from a **publisher's repository** instead | 🟢 **7 payloads over 5 Oak repositories, all first-hand** |

### 🔴 What this pass's own gates did to this pass

**`p283`'s ladder ratchet rejected `ACTION p289` twice, and both times it was right.**

1. The instrument's first ladder was uppercase stems with lowercase extensions —
   `CASE-UNVARIED/no-upper-ext`, **the identical defect `p288` was built to fix one family
   over**. Rewritten as a generated cross product; `licence` and `copying` both now grade
   `GENERATED-CASE-VARIED`.
2. 🔴 **The first fix was then measured and rejected too**: crossing stems × extensions ×
   directories took the probe from **18 requests per repository to 597**. Trimmed to **94**,
   with exhaustive recovery left to `pass275-grant-enumeration` — where `p288` proved it
   belongs, because the tree, not the ladder, is what found `bbmcps`'s lower-case `readme.md`.

🔵 **And one finding about `p283`'s audit itself:** its extractor reads an exact-word regex
alternation as path vocabulary (its own `C23` asserts that). `p289`'s classifier is the first
instrument here whose job is reading licence **prose**, so `r"full (?:licence|license) text"`
made it look like a ladder. As the character class `licen[cs]e` it grades **`COMMENT-ONLY`** —
the truth, since it has no path ladder at all.

🔵 **Also measured:** `set -u` caught `"$OUT/$safe__..."` in this pass's own probe, which bash
parses as the variable **`safe__`**. Without it, every payload would have been written to one
path and **the last one graded five times** — erasing precisely the dual-licence split the
instrument exists to find.

## Pass 284 — 2026-10-18 — **THE EIGHT-PASS RED STREAK WAS PINNING THE WRONG POPULATION, `p283`'S `NOTICE` HEADLINE WAS HALF AN INSTRUMENT ERROR, AND THE ONE LEG `p283` TOLD THIS PASS TO REPLACE BROKE A FOUR-PASS NIL**

**One-line summary:** all three of `p283`'s top items are discharged, and each one turned out to be
**wrong about itself in the same direction** — the remedy it asked for was smaller than the defect it
revealed. The census streak was a gate firing on zero risk; the `NOTICE` family was one real defect
plus one false verdict against the instrument that invented the rule; and the regional battery's
four-pass *"Africa is empty"* was a property of the query. `make hooks` was run **before any edit**
(green on `p283`'s state) and after every edit.

### 🟢 Item 1 discharged — and the eight-pass streak has a cause, not just a remedy

🔴 `p283` registered: *"DERIVE these three literals from the Makefile instead of typing them."*
🟢 Done. 🔴 **But writing it exposed why eight passes failed, and it is not forgetfulness.**

| | |
|---|---|
| the three literals | `221` test files · `40` gated · `181` ungated |
| what they pinned | **a count of FILES ON DISK** |
| what the eight added suites did to EXPOSURE | 🟢 **nothing** — p261, p262, p275, p277, p278, p279, p280 and p283 each wrote *"`ungated` stays at 181"* |
| what already caught the only at-risk shape | `--verify`'s **`UNPINNED`**, by name, with no literal involved |

🔵 **Eight consecutive passes were stopped by a red gate over a change that moved the risk by zero.**
A gate that fires on every change and on no risk trains its reader to bump the number — which is
exactly what eight passes did. 🟢 The replacement is a **cross-check between two readings of the
gate's reach, written in opposite directions**: `is_gated` walks disk files and searches the recipes;
the new `derive_gated` walks recipe lines and emits files that exist. **They agree, suite by suite,
40 = 40, with no literal anywhere** — and a **positive control injects `p280`'s exact false credit
(`p791-registry-id-provenance/test_provenance.py`) and requires the agreement to break**, so the
defect the pins uniquely caught is still caught. Suite **43 → 46**. The `71`-suite exposure
population **stays pinned**: a change there *is* a change in risk.
Evidence: [`census-derivation.2026-10-18-p284.tsv`](evidence/census-derivation.2026-10-18-p284.tsv).

### 🟢 Items 2 and 3 discharged — one real defect, one false verdict, and a ratchet instead of a pin

🔴 `p283` published *"**Not one `NOTICE` ladder on this base can find `NOTICE.TXT`**"*, `notice` being
*"the only family at **0.0 %**"*. 🟢 **Half was real. Half was the measuring instrument.**

| ladder | `p283` | 🟢 `p284` |
|---|---|---|
| `p229-grant-ladder-reach/ladder.sh` `TIER_A` | `CASE-UNVARIED` | 🟢 **`CASE-CLOSED`** — a **REAL** defect: it carried `NOTICE NOTICE.txt` only. `NOTICE.TXT` + `notice.txt` added (+2 requests/slug); `pass256-ladder-closure` green at **38/38** |
| `p1057-licence-path-case/path_case.py` | `STEM-ONLY` | 🟢 **`GENERATED-CASE-VARIED`** — 🔴 a **FALSE POSITIVE against the instrument that invented case-closure**: `candidate_paths` is a cross product over `STEMS × EXTS × _casings(stem) × {ext, ext.upper()}` and **already generates `NOTICE.TXT`** |

🔵 **Why the audit misread it — and the caveat was its own.** `p283`'s audit reads the **literal**
path vocabulary, and its docstring says so: *"An instrument that builds its paths by concatenation is
reported as what its literals show."* A cross product has no literal to read. 🔴 **The caveat sat in
the prose and was ignored at the point of publication**, which is this base's recurring shape — so it
is now **enforced in code** as a `GENERATED-CASE-VARIED` verdict whose predicate requires **both** an
extension-case and a stem-case idiom. **13 new controls in `p1057`'s own suite (16 → 29)** assert the
**generated** ladder directly. `notice` is now **1 `CASE-CLOSED`, 0 `STEM-ONLY`, 0 `CASE-UNVARIED`**.

🟢 **Item 2 as a RATCHET, not a pin** — [`ratchet.tsv`](compose/code/p283-ladder-case-audit/ratchet.tsv),
six bounds, checked in `make gate-ladder-case`. 🔵 **That choice is item 1's lesson carried across:**
an exact count goes red on every added instrument (the `p252` streak); a **floor** on good verdicts
and a **ceiling** on defective ones goes red **only on a real regression**. Base-wide `CASE-CLOSED`
**20 → 21**, `STEM-ONLY` **24 → 22**.

that is a design constraint rather than a compliance note — see

line-local predicate over a hard-wrapped corpus is that class one layer out. Quote state is tracked
across the **paragraph** now, and the real wrapped text is a control.

the output has to make that visible if it ever happens.

```
$ make claims TOKEN=conflict
ALREADY CLAIMED   conflict   STOP — read these cells before publishing an absence:
      repos/trending.md   26        intel/open-gaps.md   82       README.md   60
$ echo $?   # 1  ← the STOP signal
$ … claims zzqqxx-not-a-real-token .   →  NOT CLAIMED   (exit 0)
```

The Makefile documents that recipe as *"**THE GATE**: run before publishing any 'there is no X'"*.

shelves and 28,000+ lines, care does not substitute for running the index** — so the remedy registered
for `p279` is to make `make claims` a **step**, not a sentence in prose.

### 🔴 The most decision-relevant APAC fact is a failure, and it is the best argument this base has

**South Korea built, deployed and then unwound a national AI digital-textbook programme** — status
revoked by the National Assembly **four months into rollout** (Aug 2025); adoption 🔴 **37% → 19%**;
**two data-protection violations** found by the privacy regulator; the **state auditor found the
textbooks were brought into schools without a pilot**; publisher suits **dismissed** (Jul and Aug 2026);
the review process for 2026-year products **halted**.

🔴 **Not one cited cause was model capability** — factual errors, privacy, screen time and teacher
workload are all **implementation and governance failures, inside a delivery partner's scope.** 🟢 **It
makes three claims testable: a mandate is not adoption** (the decline happened *while* the mandate
stood), **a privacy finding outranks an accuracy benchmark**, and **the pilot is not a formality.**
New patterns **`P30`** (brief APAC per jurisdiction — there is no APAC requirement) and **`P31`** (the
pilot-gated rollout, built backwards from this reversal, with synthetic pilot data and the teacher half
shipped first). Trends **`T53`**, **`T54`**.

⚠️ **GRADE: SECONDARY-CONVERGENT, PRIMARY UNREAD — all five.** 🔴 **`mext.go.jp`, `moe.gov.sg`,
`moe.go.kr`, `cbse.gov.in`, `pib.gov.in` and `www.gov.uk` are DNS-unresolvable from this sandbox**
(`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`); only `github.com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` resolve. **This base does
not publish a licence it has not read, and it marks a regulation it could not read either.**

| `gate-enumeration` | 🔴 **FAILED** — `Error 1`, and the recipe discarded the reason | 🟢 **PASS** — `REFUTED=0 · VERIFIED-ABSENT=53 · QUEUE-UNENUMERATED=69` |
| `gate-tables` *(new this pass)* | — | 🟢 **PASS**, 15 controls |

🔴 **`p276`'s `47/47` is refuted by execution, and so are both of its expected counts** — it predicted
`VERIFIED-ABSENT=48 · QUEUE-UNENUMERATED=70`; the gate, once fixed, reports **53** and **69**. Its
*evidence* half (plain `git` + `curl` at pinned SHAs) stands; its *instrument* half was labelled
`UNVERIFIED-BY-EXECUTION`, has now been tested, and failed. 🟢 **The label is what made this measurable
in one command.**

🔴 **The gate could not say WHAT failed, because `Makefile:31` ran the suite as `>/dev/null`**,
discarding the `# N FAILING:` report the suite exists to print. **Third member of a family this Makefile
documents in its own comments:** `p253`'s gate could not **hear** its controls, `p254`'s could not

```
# 1 FAILING:

```

### 🔴 Three defects that only an EXECUTED gate could have found, and two were self-inflicted

🔴 **1. A checker anchored on the stale number cannot survive the correction it asks for.**
`recount.py` bounded the permissive-tier table with the **literal string `"**24 permissive rows"`** —
a copy of the very number under test. Correcting the shelf to `27` **deleted that boundary**, so the
measurement silently became *"every table row in the rest of the file"* and reported 🔴 **63**. The
verdict stayed `STALE` **for an entirely new reason**, which is the shape that would have survived a
careless pass: a red gate that looks like the same red gate. 🔵 **And `published` turns out to be a
Python CONSTANT, not a value read from the shelf** — so `T37` detects **row** drift and is **blind to
text** drift. Both pins moved; the claim now reads `27 / 27 / MATCH`.

🔴 **2. Adding a gate turned `gate-offline` red, exactly as designed.** `p252`'s census pins the count
of every suite on disk and every suite the Makefile reaches. Wiring `gate-tables` in moved them
`214 → 215` and `33 → 34`, and **`make hooks` went red at `p252` before a single finding had been
written up.** 🟢 **The pin was moved in the SAME change as the step** — `p261`'s remedy, `p262`'s shape
— so the census never spent a pass red. **Fifth consecutive pass where this census catches the new
instrument first.**

🔴 **3. `p261`'s ordering invariant caught a mistake of `p277`'s own, in a shelf edit rather than an

### 🔴 The defect species — and the worst part: THIS BASE ALREADY HELD THE PRINCIPLE, AND THE CODE

🔴 **The method below is not new to this base, and that is the finding.**
[`compose/code/p275-tree-enumeration/`](compose/code/p275-tree-enumeration/) — **pase 93,
`2026-10-04`** — states it outright, and ships a working blobless-clone enumerator (`sweep_tree.sh`):

> **`P275`**: *para sostener una ausencia en un árbol hay que ENUMERARLO.*
> **`P278`**: *un conteo de CERO sobre una ruta que no existe en esa ref mide la RUTA, no el contenido.*

🔴 **`P278` describes this pass's two false negatives exactly** — openSIS's grant is at a path the ladder
never spelled, Athena's at a manifest the ladder never reached — **and the principle, the corollary and
the instrument had all been sitting in `compose/code/` for ~180 passes.** They were applied to
**directory** trees (ILIAS components, `frappe`, `openeducat`) and **never to licence paths**, where the
work went on extending ladders instead: `p267`'s `19 × 4`, `p273`'s `ACTION YU`.

🔵 **`p274` wrote this pass's diagnosis and did not apply it to itself:** *"a correction applied to one
instance is not a correction to the class."* **`P275` was the correction; licences were the instance it
never reached.** **Seventh consecutive pass whose defect species was invisible to the check written one
pass earlier — and the first in which the lesson was already written on this base in GENERAL form, with
code, and was simply never carried across domains.**

🟢 **So the fix was not to invent a method. It was to apply `P275` where it had never been applied:**

```
git ls-remote <slug> HEAD                                    # positive control: does it resolve?
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --no-checkout <slug>   # blobless, seconds
git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD                               # EVERY path.  No guessing.
```

### 🔴 And the standing gate was RED at `HEAD`, which no pass-273 artefact mentions

🟢 **`p274` ran `make hooks` — and it failed, on the committed tree, before this pass had changed
anything.** Proven rather than asserted: `git stash` → the identical **6 of 166** controls fail → `git
stash pop`.

```
6/166 FAILED
  - ordering on agents/top.md is AGREE or UNDECIDABLE (reference doc)
  - agents/top.md: if it carries dated sections they are ordered
  - ordering on repos/foundations.md …            (and the same pair)
  - ordering on verticals/solutions.md …          (and the same pair)
```

🔵 **The mechanism, and it is a slow-growing defect rather than a mistake.** `p261`'s invariant is that a
shelf carrying two or more pass-numbered `##` headings must carry them **non-increasing in file order** —
the shape a shelf has when each pass **prepends**. 🔴 **These three reference docs were built by passes
that APPENDED**, so their pass numbers ran `273, 269, 268, 270, 272` (`agents/top.md`), `270, 272`
(`repos/foundations.md`) and `270, 271, 272` (`verticals/solutions.md`). **Each append was individually
harmless; the second one in ascending order tripped the invariant, and it has been red since.**

🟢 **Fixed by permuting the pass sections into descending order within their existing positions** —
content untouched, non-pass sections untouched — and `make hooks` now exits **0** with **45 PASS**.
⚠️ **One consequence recorded because it bit this pass's own prose:** the permutation **moves line
numbers**, so a finding must cite a **row and a section**, never a line number. Three of this pass's own
sentences had to be rewritten for exactly that reason.

🔴 **The deeper point is why nobody noticed.** `p261`'s own section records that the gate *"ran for the
first time in ten passes"* and was red then too; `p251` and `p252` both recorded `make` as **not runnable
from their session**. 🔵 **A gate that is only run when someone remembers is a gate whose verdict is
unknown**, and the invariant it enforces is precisely the kind no reader notices. 🟢 **`make hooks` now
also runs `make recount`** (`T43`), so the two cheapest checks on this base share one entry point.

`OpenOLAT` is the row this KB tells a studio to use when procurement excludes copyleft, so its grant

entire `TERMS AND CONDITIONS` is byte-identical to upstream**; the missing span is the **optional
APPENDIX**, replaced by two attribution notes with no legal effect. **Rider-cleared.**

that a payload *changed* between passes; it cannot say *what it says*. **Agreement "to the byte" proves
stability, not correctness.**

Of the **Sanoma Learning 2026 European Teacher Survey**, `agents/trending.md` states verbatim:

🔴 **It was in neither.** This is the **fifth cross-shelf defect in five passes** and a **new

sentence that answered the grep**, and it suppressed its own detection: `p269`'s backlog sweep
**did not list Sanoma, because this base said it was already shelved.**

*slug*; **`p270` amends the *propagation* check to grep the DESTINATION file and never to trust a
claim in the source file.** 🔵 **The same defect class turned up in a second file the same day** —

### 🔴 And the generalisation, which is the part worth taking to a client

**Five errors, and not one of them pointed toward understatement.** A mock-Senate exercise gained
the word *"Act"*. A two-year-old guidebook became the current position. A real report acquired a
cleaner title than the one it has. A two-publisher range collapsed into a point. One aggregator
citing no source became a three-country finding.

🔵 **The mechanism is compression, not carelessness.** Restatement drops **qualifiers** — status,
date, publisher, sample — and keeps the **claim**; a claim without its qualifiers reads stronger
than its evidence. 🟢 **So a client knowledge base maintained by restatement is systematically
overconfident, and the overconfidence concentrates in exactly the cells a slide quotes. The audit
that catches it is not an audit of the summary — it is re-running the original query.** Budget one
re-verification pass per six carried datums and expect roughly five to move. New trend **`T31`**.

general-purpose AI improves learning outcomes.** A **47-point gap**. 🔵 **The pitch is not "adopt
AI"**; that argument is won and the client has receipts that it did not help. It is *"the
general-purpose assistant your teachers already use does not know your curriculum, your assessment
rules or your exam board."* New trend **`T28`** and new pattern **`P20`** — the Spain/LOMLOE
teacher-workflow engagement, built on `OpenDidactia` (**CC BY-SA 4.0**, verified at payload) read as
a **specification** rather than shipped as content, with the ShareAlike boundary drawn explicitly.

🔴 **And then the premise inverts.** `-only` / `-or-later` is **SPDX's** notation. Four other grammars are in use on these shelves, and in two of them the bound is carried by **omission**:

| **Odoo** *(`*/__manifest__.py`)* | `'LGPL-3 or any later version'` | 🔴 **`'LGPL-3'` — bare IS the only-form** |
| **PyPI trove** | `… v3 or later (AGPLv3+)` | `… v3 (AGPLv3)` |
| **prose** *(a GNU header)* | *"any later version"* | *"(non-upgradable)"* |

🔴 **p221's `parse_range()` reads a bare `GPL-3` as `unspecified` in all five. ## Pass 219 — 2026-10-15 — `ACTION QV` FIRES AND ITS PREMISE INVERTS: A RECIPROCAL UPSTREAM IS A **CHANNEL HINT** BEFORE IT IS A RISK

🔵 **`1` new agent row** *(the first in `4` passes)*, **`0` new repository rows, `0` new platform rows.** 🟢 **`2` actions closed — `QV`, `QW`, both on limb `1`. `1` grant recovered first-hand against a published cell, `1` `15`-pass conflict resolved, `2` new state classes, `3` further rows answered beyond the registered population, `1` new working channel, and `3` newly blocked hosts.**

### 🆕 🟢 The headline: `ACTION QV` asked a risk question and the cheap half of it was a reading question

🔴 **`ACTION QV`, the registered highest-priority action for this pass, asked whether the `47` licence-unknown rows sit on a reciprocal upstream — *"a dead end even if the author answers."* It fires: `6` of `47` name one on a token grep, `4` of `47` are installed INTO one. Limb `1` fires on either reading, so the verdict does not rest on the adjudication.**

🔴 **Then the conclusion inverts. `3` of those `4` were never ungranted.** 🟢 **The ecosystem that makes a repo reciprocal is the same ecosystem that prescribes WHERE its licence goes — WordPress in `readme.txt` and the plugin header, Moodle in `version.php` and the file docblocks, Magento in `composer.json`. Read the channel and the dead end does not arise.**

🔴 **This reverses an order of work that has been stuck for `15` passes.** 🔴 **`ACTION PH` — *"ask the maintainer to commit a `LICENSE` body"* — would have asked `3` of these `4` authors for a file they had already shipped, under a different name, in the place their ecosystem puts it.** 🟢 **Identify the upstream → read its convention → only then consider asking a human. Written up as recipe `P219-A`.**

> repository AGPL.

🔴 **And the defect is intermittent, which is why it survives review:** the same detector read
`frappe/erpnext` correctly from an identical licence, because the two copies **wrap § 13
differently** — a line-oriented grep over wrapped legal text is not a classifier. 🟢 **The clean

for GPL-3.0 versus `15` for AGPL-3.0**, title line agreeing. `Gap 450`, `ACTION OI`.

🔵 **Why it mattered enough to re-check rather than publish:** GPL vs AGPL is the difference
between *"a client may host this"* and *"hosting it may compel disclosure."* 🟢 **The shape is
p199's own `openedx/XBlock` episode with the roles reversed — a later pass "correcting" an
earlier one that was right — and p199 wrote the rule for exactly this case.**

### 🆕 🔴 The fourth number that measured its reader: this pass's own byte counts

🔴 **Python text mode applies UNIVERSAL NEWLINES.** Reading a licence as text and reporting
`len(text.encode())` loses **one byte per CRLF line**, so the figure is the LF-normalised
length, not the file's size:

```
  BranchingScenario font LICENSE.txt   wc -c = 11 560   text-mode = 11 358   CRLF = 202
```

🟢 **`11 560 − 11 358 = 202`, exactly the CRLF count.** 🟢 **Blast radius, measured rather than
assumed: ONE row.** Every other text read this pass — all `30` root-licence rows, all `3` root
payloads, the other `13` `Lumi` texts — is LF, `delta 0`, so 🟢 **every byte figure in the
tables below stands**, and the `3` root payloads are independently confirmed byte-for-byte by
p197.

🔴 **But the band table was computed from these counts**, so a CRLF row would have shifted a
ratio silently. 🟢 **The fix is in `p198-title-line-family/`: read in BINARY, report `len(raw)`,
and report the CRLF count alongside it** so a reflowed text is visible as reflowed rather than
showing up as a band failure. 🔵 [`evidence/crlf-byte-undercount.2026-10-14-p198.tsv`](evidence/crlf-byte-undercount.2026-10-14-p198.tsv).

🔵 **The lesson, and it is the same one three times over now:** `GPL-2.0`'s preamble made a
*window* report the wrong family; a filename list made a *first match* report the wrong file;
text mode made a *byte count* report the wrong size. 🟢 **Every one is a reader's property
published as the world's.**

### 🔴 `Gap 433` — the record is protected; the ACTOR is not. Two codebases, same omission.

| | the record | the actor |
|---|---|---|
| [`openfun/ralph`](https://github.com/openfun/ralph) 🟢 `MIT` *(🆕 `LICENSE.md` `1 094` B — `LICENSE` itself `404`s)* | 🟢 `409 CONFLICT` on **both** write paths, raised before the backend write, documented in a source comment | 🔴 `statements_are_equivalent` compares `{actor, verb, object, id, result, context, attachments}` + `timestamp`/`version` **only when in both** — and excludes **`authority`** and `stored` by name |

one.** *"Nobody protects the record"* is refutable by anyone who has read either codebase.
🟢 ***"The record is protected and the actor is not"*** is true in both, demonstrable from
source, and it is exactly what a regulator, a DPO or an exam board asks — because a trail
that cannot say **who** is not a trail. 🟢 **Pattern `36` is the response**, and steps `1`–`4`
are a READ, so they quote at fixed price.

🔵 **On `ralph` the consequence is not the one the falsifier predicted.** Because equivalence

everything under it: right for pedagogy, wrong for audit.** 🟢 Three regimes now require that
record — NA *(Oklahoma, Maryland)*, EU *(high-risk assessment)* and 🔴 **Vietnam, the second
jurisdiction to put educational assessment in a statutory high-risk tier.** 🟢 Pattern `32` is the
fix, and step `2` — moving the log out of the course aggregate — is the whole value.

  *"O'Saasy License Agreement"* is MIT verbatim plus an anti-SaaS non-compete. 🔴 **Not open
  source**, and 🔴 **every body-matching classifier on this shelf returns `MIT` for it.** 🟢 New
  instrument, `14` tests passing, validated against live bytes:
  [`compose/code/p1054-mit-plus-clause`](compose/code/p1054-mit-plus-clause/README.md).

  MIT measured at `1 062`–`1 093` B over `15` genuine rows; `graspful` is `1 439`)*.

  `moodle-block_atrisk` *(`GPL-3` in `703` B)*. 🔵 Say **"by reference"**, not "Apache-2.0" — §`3`,
  the patent grant, is the only strong reason to prefer it and it travels as a URL.

  measured nothing. Run a known-positive through any sweep before believing it.**

### 🔴 `P146-D` — the finding this pass exists for

`P145-A` is the strongest finding this shelf has produced: an exclusion list four lines
above the one being audited had removed seven of eight rows from a tier, and what was left
behind looked like a measurement. p145 fixed it in its successor and named the class `T42`.

🔴 **What p145 did not ask is whether anything else on the shelf could do the same, or
whether anything would notice.** Both answers are bad.

| | count |
|---|---|
| instruments that traverse a tree | **35** |
| …that carry an **empty-walk guard** | 🔴 **0** |
| …that exclude `dist`/`build`, have no re-admission, and emit a verdict | 🔴 **5** |
| …that cannot read anything but a git clone | 🔴 **16** |

🔵 **The exclusion list was one instrument's bug; the inability to notice is the shelf's.**
A guard is four lines and needs no judgement, because the question it asks has one right
answer in every artefact kind: *did I read anything at all?* `p146-empty-walk-guard`
answers it, and `walked_or_refuse` is wired to preserve the distinction that `P145-A`'s
seven rows collapsed —

| state | meaning | correct output |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **zero files walked** | the instrument saw no input | **no verdict is available** |
| 🟢 **files walked, none matched** | the instrument saw input and found no surface | `NOT_AN_MCP_SERVER` — a finding |

🔴 **`P145-A`'s rows were the first state, published as the second**, and `P146-B` shows a
second instrument standing ready to do it again on the agent tier.

it is a third distinct blocker, alongside `P139`'s execution refusal and `P144-V`'s DNS

### 🔴 `P145-A` — the finding this pass exists for

`ACTION DZ` was registered on a correct observation: `surface_gate2.py` reads **0** on real
MCP servers that register through `setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, …)`. 🟢 **The
repair was built and it works.** 🔴 **It is not why seven rows read zero.**

`SKIP_DIRS` at `surface_gate2.py:79` contains `dist` and `build`, and `shipped_only` adds
`NOT_SHIPPED` on top rather than changing it. So both modes drop both trees — and the npm
tier keeps all of its code in them:

|---|---|
| 🔴 `dist/` | `@imazhar101/mcp-canvas-server` (69 files), `moodle-mcp-server-aql` (68), `@ink-waffle/moodle-mcp` (18), `mcp-canvas-lms` (16) |

| 🟢 `lib/` + root | `@n35da/brightspace-mcp` (17) — 🟢 **the only row p143 measured** |

🔵 **This is `T39` one level up from where `P144-O` applied it.** `NOT_SHIPPED` was audited
in p143, p144 and p145. 🔴 **`SKIP_DIRS` sat four lines above it and was never read** — and
it was doing the consequential filtering: removing seven of eight rows from a tier and
leaving behind something shaped like a measurement. 🆕 **That is `T42`.**

probe's two deliberate changes. 🟢 **And five of the seven new readings match counts this KB
already held from unrelated instruments**, which is what makes the corrections trustworthy
rather than merely different.

### `P139-B` — why the write axis is the finding and the count is not

An undocumented read tool is a missing paragraph. 🔴 **An undocumented `bulk_update_grades` is an
ungoverned capability** — and *"grading or ranking learners"* is named high-risk by **EU AI Act
Annex III** and by **Vietnam's Decision 33/2026/QĐ-TTg**, the only education-AI conformity regime
actually in force (`T16`). 🔵 **A duty cannot be discharged against a capability nobody has
enumerated, and the README is what procurement reads.** That is why this pass adds **`P18`**, a
gate, rather than a caveat on `P17`: pull the payload, count registered tools across all three
registration idioms, diff against the documentation, partition by write verb, then call `tools/list`
on the running server and diff again — because registration is not behaviour.

🔴 **`@imazhar101/mcp-canvas-server` is the row that should stop a delivery conversation**: 227
tools, 96 documented, **61 undocumented writes**, including **`update_sso_settings`** and
**`restore_authentication_provider`** — tools that change how a Canvas tenant authenticates — in the
same package p138 found carrying **no licence signal and no `repository` field**, so there is no
source to audit either.

### `P139-C` — the one that changes delivery, and it moved the cost rather than removing it

p138 wrote of its own `ACTION CE`: *"answered by reading an interface, not by calling it."* `ACTION CL`
called it. 🟢 **The brokered flow does not demand the Canvas redirect when a grant is pre-seeded** —
proven by a sentinel listener standing in for Canvas and recording **zero** connections, with the
grant store encrypted at rest (`scrypt` + AES-GCM, no plaintext). 🔴 **But the integration shape is
not what p138 implied**: because `main()` runs on import, an embedder cannot pass `oauthStore` in
process. The working route is **seed the encrypted store, run `serve` as a managed process**. `P13`
is rewritten a fifth time: 🟢 **protocol work drops to hours, plumbing rises to ~a week**, and the
"no fork" claim is **narrowed, not refuted** — no fork to *use* it, a one-line `main` guard to
*embed* it.

### `P138-A` — why the layer is the finding

🔵 **This KB has read licence files at four layers: the root file, tree enumeration, source headers,
registry metadata. The payload is the fifth, and it is the only one a client receives.**
`npm install` unpacks a tarball; it does not clone a repository. A grant that lives only at HEAD is
never conveyed to the person who installs — so a licence cell can be correct about a repository and
wrong about the delivery.

🟢 **Direction of the error is recorded because it decides the remedy.** All nine defective rows are
the repository being *better* than the distribution. **Not one package shipped a licence its
repository lacked.** So this is packaging discipline, not misrepresented licensing, and the ask to
an upstream is a one-line `files` change. 🟢 **That asymmetry became a pattern**: `P17`, the
licence-payload gate, with the fail/warn/block split drawn along it.

🔵 **The defect is invisible to the tools a studio already runs.** `npm ls --json` and any scanner
that reads `package.json` both report `MIT` for a package whose tarball contains no licence text.

Probe, method, committed 21-row TSV and **7 passing tests**:
[`compose/code/p138-npm-payload-licence`](compose/code/p138-npm-payload-licence/README.md).

### `P138-D` — the one that changes delivery, not just the ledger

🔵 **`P13` has been rewritten four times: build (p135) → buy-and-adapt (p136) → adapter (p137) → a
named interface (p138).** This pass is the one where the remaining work stopped being an estimate:
`CanvasMCPServerConfig` accepts an embedder-supplied `OAuthStore`, so the adapter seeds a `Grant`
carrying the per-user Canvas refresh token — in the shape
[`kstateome/lti-launch`](https://github.com/kstateome/lti-launch) proves — and the brokered flow
issues an audience-bound MCP token **without forking `ltijs` or `canvas-lms-mcp`**.

🔴 **Not refuted: the adapter is still required.** The subject is established by `CanvasOAuthClient`,
which redirects the user to Canvas; no code path accepts an external verified assertion. 🔴 And
`store.ts` carries *"Update only, never create (QA S7, #356)"* on the Canvas-refresh path, so the
grant must be created up front rather than lazily.

### `P137-A` — the finding, and why it lands on the same spot twice

🔵 **p136 wrote this pass's target in its own words**: *"Nothing maps a verified LTI 1.3 launch onto
a broker's subject and audience… this is the whole remaining bespoke surface of the sanctioned
path."* `ACTION BX` was registered to test that before it was asserted as fact — the same discipline
that refuted `ACTION BS` one pass earlier.

🔴 **It is refuted in source.** `kstateome/lti-launch` — LGPL-3.0, **Kansas State University, Office
of Mediated Education**, 34 paths, HEAD 2026-09-30 — does exactly the mapping, and has for years:

- `LtiLaunch.ensureApiTokenPresent()` reads the **launch subject** from the LTI session
  (`ltiSession.getEid()`);
- it looks up a **per-user** refresh token through `OauthTokenService.getRefreshToken(userId)`;
- when there is none, `OauthController./beginOauth` redirects **that user** to
  `https://<canvas>/login/oauth2/auth` with a per-session `state` UUID, and the callback stores
  `storeToken(userId, refreshToken)`;
- the resulting `RefreshableOauthToken` then calls Canvas **as that user**, validated by
  `showUserDetails("self")`.

🟡 **What survives is narrow and exact, and it is now measured rather than assumed.** The mapping is
anchored on an **LTI 1.1** launch (OAuth 1.0a consumer signing — `LtiOAuthAuthenticationHandler`,
`LtiConsumerDetailsService`), and it hands back a *platform API* token, not an **RFC 8707**-bound
token for an MCP resource server. The 1.3 half of the gap is confirmed in the canonical library's
own code: `ltijs` **v7.0.7**'s `AccessTokenManager` mints only
`grant_type=client_credentials` with the assertion `{sub: platform.clientId, iss: platform.clientId,
aud: platform.authorizationServer}` — 🔴 **the tool's own client id is the subject**, the launching
user's `sub` is stored (`idTokenDoc.user`) and never leaves, and the token cache is keyed by
platform + client + scopes, never by user. 🔴 And 1EdTech's own reference tool
([`1EdTech/lti-1-3-php-example-tool`](https://github.com/1EdTech/lti-1-3-php-example-tool)) has a
HEAD of **2020-06-03** and returns a hard-coded UUID string as its `access_token`.

🟢 **So `P13` drops again — from p136's "three-to-four-week buy-and-adapt" to an adapter of
about two weeks** between three components that each already exist, and `T13` is rewritten for the
second pass running. The seam is named in `compose/patterns.md` → `P13`.

### `P137-B` and `P137-J` — the two reads that cut in opposite directions

🟢 **`ACTION CA` predicted its own refutation and got it**: all three connectors added-but-unread by
p136 match their descriptions, so the 2-for-2 defect streak belongs to the rows p135 read, not to the
tier. 🔵 **But each read still changed a model this KB publishes**: the password-credential tier is a
**deployment configuration** rather than a property of a repository (`brightspace-mcp-server` ships a
passwordless mode and a token-paste path beside the keychain one); a 136-tool vendor connector with
`edubase_delete_organization` in it turns out to carry **`EDUBASE_READONLY`, per-toolset selection
and MCP `destructiveHint` annotations**, which is the best-governed write surface on this shelf; and
a **9★** repository is a fuller OAuth 2.1 implementation than anything the 289★ fork family contains.

🔴 **`P137-J` is the inverse of p136's `pipwerks` correction.** There, a row this KB called
unlicensed turned out to carry a grant **outside** the filename probe. Here, the row carries an
SPDX identifier in `package.json` — `"license": "MIT"`, a real identifier, and `"LICENSE"` listed in
`files` — while **tree enumeration over all 36 paths finds no licence file at all**. 🔵 **The class
is new and it is the one that matters for redistribution: an SPDX id without text.** A client told
to "ship the notice" has nothing to ship.

### `P135-A` — the finding, and why it is a component rather than a caveat

🔵 **It was only answerable because the channel changed.** Earlier passes read *payloads*; this one
**cloned the repositories** (`git clone --depth 1`, all three succeeded) and read the implementation.

🟢 **What the source confirms.** `Cvmcosta/ltijs` holds **no user credential at all** — the only
secret is a platform-issued `client_credentials` token, cached per `platformUrl`+`clientId`+`scopes`,
that the institution can revoke. User identity comes from an `id_token` whose signature is
**verified** against the platform's keys, with nonce tracking. `bb-mcp` keeps tokens **in memory
only** and authenticates with an institution-issued app secret. `learnmcp-xapi` uses an **LRS
service credential**. 🔴 **Not one of the three stores a student's password**, which is exactly the
distinction that makes the 36-row portal tier unshippable and this tier shippable.

🔴 **What the source refutes.** `bb-mcp` requires a `caller_identity` argument on every tool call and
its README states plainly: *"This identity is trusted at face value (bb-mcp does not itself verify
end-user identity)"*; `MCP_API_KEY` authenticates **the client, not the user**, and `role: "admin"`
**bypasses** the course-entitlement gate that otherwise stops a grade write into an unenrolled
course. `learnmcp-xapi` takes its actor from `ACTOR_UUID` in the environment at all three call sites
— 🔴 **and two of its own docstrings say *"Actor UUID from JWT"* while the project has no JWT
dependency at all.** The code is honest; its comments describe a trust anchor it does not have.

🟢 **So the gap is a named, small, unbuilt component:** an **identity broker** that terminates a
verified identity (LTI launch, OIDC, or the institution's IdP) and only then calls the MCP server
with a subject it established itself. Nothing in this KB does it, in any region. Written up as
`compose/patterns.md` → **P13**, pre-registered as `ACTION BS` to probe before the absence is
asserted as fact.

### `P135-B` — the register, and the variable nobody had isolated

`ACTION BN` finished the six remaining standards. 🔴 **Maturity tracks the standard's AGE, not its
design**: SCORM (1999) is technically the crudest of the six and carries four repositories above
350★; **Caliper (2015) is the most modern event model and has one repository, 0 stars, no licence,
untouched since 2023**; Comprehensive Learner Record has **one real row**. 🟢 **The mechanism is
installed base, not merit** — institutions have *bought* SCORM and LTI for twenty years, so there is
something to write against.

🔴 **This changes what can be promised.** *"We build on sanctioned standards"* is credible for
content and launch, defensible for assessment and credentials, and **not currently true for
analytics**. Eleven institution- or vendor-owned rows were added, against `ACTION BN`'s refutation
threshold of three: **Newcastle University** (`Numbas`), **Stichting Cito** (`qti-convert`, holder
read out of its own filled-in GPL appendix), **1EdTech itself**, **ADL / US DoD** (archived and
unlicensed), **SURF** (archived), EPAM, Longsight, amp-up.io, AgencyEnterprise, Impierce, Selleo.

### `P135-E`–`P135-G` — `ACTION BP`, and why a licence badge is only a lead

🔴 **A licence payload never hashes to its canonical text naively.** SPDX wraps at ~105 columns;
real `LICENSE` files wrap at ~72. **Zero of 26 payloads were whitespace variants**, refuting BP's
premise outright. The classes that actually defeat identity, in order of how often they bit: **line
wrap**, **typographic punctuation** (SPDX's GPL-3.0 uses curly quotes; shipped `COPYING` files use
ASCII), **steward edits to the licence's own text**, **appendix instantiation**, **undated notices**.

🔴 **`P135-G` is the part worth carrying into any future instrument.** Removing copyright notices
line-by-line is **wrap-dependent in both possible orders**, and each order silently deleted real
licence text rather than failing loudly — strip after reflow and GNU's *"Everyone is permitted…"*
goes with the notice it shares a paragraph with; strip before reflow and Apache-2.0's *"…a readable
copyright notice that is included in or attached to the work"* is deleted because a 72-column break
lands in front of the word `copyright`. Both were observed on real payloads in this corpus. The
rule: **remove a notice as a span inside an already-reflowed paragraph, anchored at the paragraph
start, requiring a year — or, if the paragraph is nothing but a notice, without one.**

🟢 **And the practical edge:** a badge would have mislabelled an LMS a studio *can* use
(`OpenOLAT`, permissive) and said nothing about two it cannot — `pipwerks/scorm-api-wrapper`
(**391★, 130 forks, no licence file at all**) and `cybercussion/SCOBot` (**164★, CC-BY-SA-4.0, and
the file is only the human-readable deed**).

### `P134-A` / `P134-B` — the finding, and why it is a build rather than a dependency

🔵 **The probe that found it was `grade passback`, then `lti 1.3 advantage`, `oneroster`, `ltijs` and
`xapi` — the professional register of the people who do this work for a living.** Not the category
term (`SIS`, which found nothing for p132), not the capability term (`timetable`, which found p132's
21 rows), not a national platform noun (which found p133's 15). 🟢 **It is a fourth, distinct
vocabulary, and it is the one that reaches institutional and vendor-owned supply** — clause 5 in
`agents/top.md`.

🟢 **What it reached.** `Cvmcosta/ltijs` (**Apache-2.0**, payload-read, **373★**, pushed 2026-10-06)
— the platform-independent LTI 1.3 Advantage tool provider with OIDC launch, Deep Linking, **AGS
grade passback** and NRPS rosters. Plus `pylti1.3` (MIT, 138★), `trilogy-group/oneroster-ts`
(**0BSD** — the most permissive licence in this KB, it drops even attribution),
`Ed-Fi-Alliance-OSS/edfi-oneroster` (**Apache-2.0**, the standards body's own bridge, pushed
2026-10-09), `googleworkspace/oneroster-integration-conformance-tests` (**Apache-2.0** — 🟢 **the
only conformance suite this KB has found for any standard in this industry**), and
`AlexMeiling/wiseflow-api-integration-packages` (**MIT**, holder **"UNIwise ApS"** — the WISEflow
vendor itself).

🔴 **A tool launched over LTI holds no user credential at all.** It runs on a client ID the
institution issued and can revoke. **That is the whole answer to the blocker this KB has been
documenting**, and it is also why `st22209/Parent-Portal`'s death certificate
(*"DEPRECATED AFTER KAMAR API CHANGE"*) does not apply to it.

🔴 **And here is the gap, which is sharper and more valuable than the one it replaces: the standards
are finished and the agents have not arrived.** The bridge from an agent to any sanctioned standard
is **one repository** — `DavidLMS/learnmcp-xapi` (MIT, 15★, last push 2025-08-29) — and the only
Ed-Fi MCP server in existence is **an empty repository**:

| `size` | 🔴 **0** |
| raw lane, **15 probes** (5 entry points × `HEAD` / `main` / `master`) | 🔴 **404 on all fifteen** |
| `created_at` / `pushed_at` | 🔴 **`2026-02-17T19:54:46Z` / `:47Z`**, never touched again |

🔵 **`size: 0` plus a 404 sweep is a measurement of emptiness.** A pass that trusted the description
would have tabled a working Ed-Fi MCP server that does not exist — the easiest way this KB could

compliance clocks (EU **2027-12-02**, Oklahoma **before 2027-28**, Maryland **June 2027**).

### `P133-A` — why two timestamps one second apart settle it

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `instructure/canvas-lms` → `topics` | **`canvas-lms`, `gerrit-mirror`, `instructure`** |
| `instructure/canvas-lms` → `pushed_at` | **2026-04-30T14:52:10Z** |
| `instructure/analytics` → `pushed_at` | **2026-04-30T14:52:11Z** |
| `instructure/canvas-lms` → `updated_at` | **2026-10-11** (today) |

🔵 **Two independent repositories cannot be hand-pushed one second apart.** A timestamp shared to
the second is a batch job, and the repo's own topic names what kind. 🔴 **So "Canvas went quiet in
April" was never a statement about Instructure's activity — it is the date their export to GitHub
stopped running.** The correct claim is narrower and more useful to a client: **the public mirror has
been frozen for five months, GitHub is therefore not an activity signal for Canvas, and anyone
diffing this tree to track upstream has been reading a stale copy.**

🟡 **This does not rehabilitate Canvas as a contribution target** — a Gerrit-upstream AGPL-3.0
project with a frozen mirror is *harder* to build on. It changes what the KB may infer from
`pushed_at`, which it has been inferring project health from in two lanes. 🔴 **`ACTION BG` opened:
every mirror in `git-recency-channel` and `p109-freshness` is currently mis-ranked toward looking
abandoned.** 🔵 **The diagnosis came from one control request — pulling a *second* repo from the same
org — not from new search coverage.**

(`get_file_contents`) is **scope-blocked in this session** — it returns *"repository is not
configured for this session"* for every repo but this KB's own. **That is an authorisation refusal,
not a 404 and not evidence about the repo**, and a pass that logged it as "no licence file" would
publish a fabricated absence. 🟢 **Working lane: `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/LICENSE`.**

### `P132-A` — why every previous pass's SIS query returned zero

🔵 **The field is not organised by the category term. It is organised by platform name.** This KB
searched for *"student information system"*, *"school management"*, *"SIS"* — the words an analyst
uses. The people actually building these connectors name them after the system they connect to:
**Librus** (Poland), **EduPage** (Slovakia), **Pronote** (France), **IServ** (Germany), **Sisu**
(Finland), **uSaint** (South Korea), **VTOP** (India), **QLDT** (Vietnam), **VSB** / **Quercus**
(Canada), **NYCU** (Taiwan).

🔴 **So p131's `P131-E` was right about the mechanism and still understated it.** p131 found that a
multi-term query returns a zero that measures the query. This pass shows the stronger version: **the
category term itself can be absent from an entire real field**, because the builders are not
analysts. A query built from the analyst's vocabulary cannot see them at any star threshold.

🟢 **And the builders are not enterprises — they are students and parents.** Nearly every row is one
person connecting an assistant to their own university or their own child's school. That explains
every property of the tier at once: tiny star counts, MIT licences chosen by default, precise
regional placement, brand-new creation dates, and **no procurement story whatsoever**.

### `P132-B` — the tier inverts two things this KB has said for many passes

| standing KB claim | what this tier shows |
|---|---|
| *"Most agent repos carry no location evidence at all — 11 of the 17 rows are unplaced rather than guessed"* (`intel/market.md`) | 🟢 **~90% of the 21 new rows are placed on hard evidence** — a named university, a national platform, a country-coded homepage (`mine.ibu.edu.ba`, `qldt.hanu.edu.vn`). Region is *stated*, not inferred |
| *"The permissive/popular inversion, across every tier measured this pass… the most-starred item is repeatedly the unusable one"* (`intel/market.md`) | 🔴 **Inverted back.** ~80% of this tier is **MIT**. The exceptions are small: one GPL-2.0, one Apache-2.0, three unlicensed. 🟡 **But the tier's own top two by stars are the weak ones** — `librus-mcp` (10★) is mixed-licence and `DAU-buddy` (7★) is unlicensed |

🔵 **The honest reading of both:** this KB's generalisations were drawn from one tier — big, famous,
Canvas-and-Moodle-shaped repos — and do not survive contact with a second. **A claim about "every
tier measured" is only ever a claim about the tiers you queried.**

### `P132-C` — the pattern this KB wrote as an opportunity already exists at 39 444 stars

`intel/trends.md` → T8 and `compose/patterns.md` → P2 have called offline/low-bandwidth delivery
*"the most valuable unfilled slot in the whole KB"* and *"the clearest unclaimed opportunity"*, on
the strength of a probe that found **86 repos named `kolibri`, 3 in the family, 0 with AI**.

🔴 **The probe was sound and the conclusion was wrong, because the occupant is not named after
Kolibri.** [`Crosstalk-Solutions/project-nomad`](https://github.com/Crosstalk-Solutions/project-nomad)
— **Apache-2.0, 39 444★** — is an offline-first knowledge and education server that orchestrates
containerised tools via Docker: **Kiwix** powers its Information Library, **Kolibri** powers its
Education Platform, and **Ollama** powers its AI Assistant.

🔵 **That is pattern `P2`, line for line, built and permissively licensed.** It is the
second-largest repository anywhere in this KB — behind only `HKUDS/DeepTutor` (41 136★) — and no
pass had seen it, because every Kolibri probe searched for the string `kolibri` in names and
descriptions, and NOMAD's description does not contain it.

**Consequence for an engagement, stated plainly:** the offline opportunity is **not** greenfield.
It is now *"extend, contribute to, or deploy a 39k-star Apache-2.0 stack"* — a far better starting
position than the build P2 described, and a completely different conversation with a client.

### `P132-D` — the market spread was an artefact of mixing base years

This KB's headline has been: *2026 estimates span ~$6.4B to ~$11.4B, a **1.8× spread for the
current year**, so quote the range and the disagreement.* 🔴 **One row in that table is not a 2026
estimate.** IMARC's **~$6.4B is a 2025 base** (its own earlier edition reads $4.8B for 2024 →
$75.1B by 2033).

🟢 **Restrict the table to figures genuinely for 2026 and the firms nearly agree: $9.58B, $10.4B,
$10.6B, ~$11B — a 1.19× spread.** The real disagreement is not about today at all; it is about the
horizon, where 2035 estimates run from **~$70B to ~$1 169B (~17×)**. One source even publishes two
different CAGRs for its own forecast (34.52% and 36.02%).

🔵 **This reverses the advice.** "Nobody agrees what this market is worth now" was wrong and
unsellable. **"The firms agree within ~20% on the current year and diverge seventeen-fold by 2035"**
is both true and a much sharper thing to say in a commercial conversation.

### `P132-E` — the instrument's second blind spot, and it is the opposite of the first

p131 established that a **generic zero** measures the query. This pass establishes the mirror
image: **a generic enormous number measures the query too.**

| query as written | intent | returned |
|---|---|---|
| `oneroster OR ed-fi MCP agent in:name,description` | the rostering-standard connector tier | 🔴 **69 812** — the global MCP-agent population |
| `swahili OR yoruba OR amharic education in:name,description` | African-language education repos | 🔴 **248 136** — the global `education` population |
| `arabic education LLM tutor in:name,description stars:>5` | MENA tutoring | 🔴 **0** |
| `arabic LLM in:name,description stars:>50` *(control)* | — | 🟢 **3**, one of them a **63★ student-facing advisor** |

🔴 **`OR` is not honoured as a boolean here.** It does not union two narrow sets; it collapses the
query into a broad match. **So a result count in this instrument is evidence of nothing until the
query form is checked** — a zero, a 69 812 and a 248 136 can all be artefacts. `ACTION BC` (a named
control beside every declared absence) is hereby extended: **a named control beside every declared
abundance as well.**

### `P132-F` — the new rule caught a real grant within one pass of being written

p131 ruled KB-wide that **`NOASSERTION` means "GitHub's matcher did not recognise this file" — it
is UNREAD, never UNGRANTED**, and told later passes to read the payload.
[`zavora-ai/mcp-student-records`](https://github.com/zavora-ai/mcp-student-records) came back
`NOASSERTION` from the API. 🟢 **The payload is Apache-2.0**, holder *"Copyright 2026 Zavora AI"*.

🔵 **And the mechanism is new and worth naming.** The `LICENSE` file is **not** a truncated or
bespoke licence — it is the **~745-byte Apache-2.0 *notice block*** (the "Licensed under the Apache
License, Version 2.0… you may obtain a copy at apache.org" stanza) **without the licence body**.
GitHub's matcher needs the body, so it reports "Other". 🟡 **Flag for counsel, not a blocker:** the
grant is by incorporation-by-reference, which is ordinary practice, but a client's reviewer will
want the full text vendored before shipping a derivative.

🟢 **It also answers one instance of this KB's standing `ACTION AY`** (*"who grants the 46
Apache-2.0 / ECL rows with no licensor"*): this row **has** a named licensor, and it is an
organisation rather than an individual — the only org-owned row in the new SIS tier.

🔵 **Region recorded honestly:** EMEA on the strength of its *stated target audience* (Egyptian
students) and its Arabic-first design. **The author's own location is not established** by anything

🟡 **So the gap narrows rather than closes:** the region is no longer *"no evidence found"*. It is
*"one 63★ row, aimed at Egypt, that nobody may build on."* Also noted:
[`mbzuai-oryx/ClimateGPT`](https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/ClimateGPT) (80★, **MBZUAI, Abu Dhabi**,

# 📚 Education KB

> Knowledge base de la industria **Education** para Globant AI Studios.
> Tutores AI, evaluación automática, personalización del aprendizaje, LMS agents

## Estructura

```
education-kb/
├── agents/        # Agentes AI open source de la industria
├── repos/         # Repos MIT/Apache como punto de partida
```

### 🔴 Una hipótesis que este pase FORMÓ, PROBÓ y REFUTÓ

🔵 **La hipótesis:** el código de scoring es permisivo y los corpus corregidos son no-comerciales, así
que el corpus es el bloqueo real. 🔴 **Refutada con n = 3:**
`anaistack/cefr-asag-corpus` es **CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0** (leído del payload, `LICENSE.txt` 20 863 B),
🟢 ASAP 2.0 se reporta **CC BY**, y 🔴 **PERSUADE 2.0 lo tiene DISPUTADO: el distribuidor dice
CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 y el originador dice CC BY 4.0.**
🟢 **Lo que reemplaza a la regla es más angosto y más útil:** la licencia del corpus es el término que
decide un proyecto de respuesta abierta, **no es uniforme**, y en el corpus más grande **el
distribuidor y el originador la declaran distinto**. 🔴 **No se pudo zanjar — las dos páginas están en
el conjunto rechazado — así que queda como `Gap 389`.** 🔵 **Una licencia de corpus es un término de
compra: nunca heredarla del listado de un distribuidor.**

### 🟢 El número que esta KB venía argumentando sin tener: 31,9 % → 0,2 %

El estudio de anclaje de `bncc-benchmark` (**8 modelos, 300 ítems**): **31,9 %** de alucinación sin fuente en
contexto · **0,2 %** con el dataset en el prompt · **2,3 %** consultando el servidor MCP.
🟢 **Anclar vale ~160× en esta tarea**, y 🔴 **la vía MCP es diez veces peor que embeber** aunque siga siendo
~14× mejor que nada. 🔵 **Decisión de arquitectura con evidencia: para alineación curricular, embebé el
dataset y dejá la llamada a herramienta para la cola larga.** La fidelidad sin anclaje va de **88 % a 3 %**
según el modelo, así que *"qué modelo"* es una palanca mucho más débil que *"¿está la fuente en el
contexto?"*. `T11`, costeado en `P93-B`.
🟡 **Citarlo con cuidado, por razones que el repo declara él mismo:** 🟢 su README **declara el conflicto de
interés** (*"a Profy opera produtos que usam LLMs sobre a BNCC"*) y publica metodología, ítems y respuestas
crudas para recalcular; 🔴 **y sus dos superficies se contradicen en el tamaño del corpus** (descripción:
15 300 respuestas/17 modelos; README: 19 modelos × 900 = 17 100). 🔵 **Citar los porcentajes, no el tamaño
del corpus.** 🔴 **Límite: un benchmark, un currículo, un idioma, 300 ítems — la dirección generaliza, la
magnitud no.**

### 🔴 Dos defectos nuevos de alcance, y uno lo confirma un segundo oráculo

- 🆕 🔴 **`P969` — el escalador de licencias lee SOLO nombres en la raíz.** `bncc-dev/bncc-dados` publica
  **MIT en la raíz** mientras **los datos bajo `dados/` son CC BY 4.0**, y `LICENSE-DADOS.md` en la raíz es
  **404**. 🔴 **La barra lateral de licencias de GitHub dice lo mismo que el escalador: "MIT license".**
  🔵 **Dos oráculos independientes, un punto ciego, una causa: detección solo en la raíz** — por eso es un
  hallazgo sobre el método y no un defecto de un script. 🟢 **Y el mismo publicador muestra el arreglo en sus
  otros dos repos:** un índice de concesión dividida **en la raíz**, con cada licencia acotada a rutas
  explícitas. **La convención, no la herramienta, es lo que hace legible una concesión dividida.**
  🔴 **`Gap 370`**: `compose/code/p199-perfile-license/` ya hace sondeo por ruta y **no está conectado** al
  escalador; el caso que falla queda comiteado en `compose/code/p969-root-only-licence-reach/`.
- 🆕 🔴 **`P971` — un archivo `LICENSE` puede ser el AVISO de cabecera de Apache, no la LICENCIA.**
  [`wwrwbs/AI_AWE`](https://github.com/wwrwbs/AI_AWE): **1 865 B** contra los **11 357 B** canónicos, 29
  líneas no vacías, bloque de título correcto y el aviso *"obtain a copy at <URL>"*. 🔴 **Un grep no
  encuentra "Grant of Patent License", "Grant of Copyright License", "Redistribution", "trademark" ni
  "APPENDIX".** 🔵 **La concesión existe por referencia, pero los términos no están en el repositorio** — y
  **la única razón fuerte para preferir Apache sobre MIT es §3, la concesión de patente, que viaja como URL.**
  🔴 **Invisible a todo instrumento de este estante**, porque un clasificador de bloque de título devuelve
  `Apache-2.0` y no se equivoca.

🟢 **Y `P965` sobrevive a un payload para el que no fue construido.** Su umbral medido (*una concesión real
nombra 0–2 familias; un marco nombra 3, de tres linajes*) separa correctamente los índices de `bncc-dev`
—nombran **2**, y **son** concesiones reales, con los textos referenciados verificados presentes— del
`LICENSE.md` de `learning-commons-org/knowledge-graph`, que no concede nada. **Misma forma de documento,
usabilidad opuesta.**

  registro.**
- 🔴 **Y el tamaño de mercado: el desacuerdo ahora está DENTRO de una sola firma.** La serie regional de
  MarketsandMarkets (NA **951 M USD**, Europa **512,6 M**, APAC **591,6 M**, resto de LATAM **18,2 M**, todos
  2024) **suma ≈ 2,07 mil millones**, contra una banda 2026 de **7–11,4 mil millones** de las firmas de la
  tabla. 🔵 **Dos años de 40 % no cierran esa brecha: el problema es el ALCANCE, no la fecha.** 🔴 **No se
  puede cerrar**: `marketsandmarkets.com` está bloqueado por el allowlist de egreso y ninguna firma de la
  serie alta publica desglose geográfico. 🟢 **Regla nueva: nunca poner un tamaño de mercado en un deck de
  educación sin nombrar el alcance al lado.**

### 🔴 El hueco más consecuente que este pase abrió

🔴 **`Gap 372`: no existe librería permisiva y de grado productivo para corrección automática de ensayos.**
Toda la oferta permisiva es **un repo de investigación de 2★** con la licencia de `P971`. 🔵 **Es decir: la
actividad que el AI Act nombra de alto riesgo de forma más explícita es la que tiene menos oferta abierta.**
`P93-A` la deja fuera de alcance explícitamente en vez de prometerla.

## Pase 92 — 2026-10-10 (resumen)

🔴 **El instrumento del pase 91 bifurcó el clasificador de licencias y reescribió mal una licencia que esta
KB YA HABÍA CORREGIDO; el valor equivocado llegó hasta una recomendación de engagement.**
`oat-sa/tao-core` y `portabilis/i-educar` se publicaron como **LGPL-3.0** y son **GPL-2.0** — y *"link,
don't absorb"* es un consejo que solo existe para LGPL. Mecanismo (`P960`): el preámbulo canónico de
GPL-2.0 referencia la LGPL en el byte ~847, dentro de la ventana, y la copia bifurcada probaba
`"gnu lesser"` **antes** de `"gnu general public"`. 🟢 Corregido en tres archivos; `grant-ladder-v4` no
tiene clasificador propio (`P237`); tres reparaciones llevadas **aguas arriba** a la librería compartida
(`P962` CC0 inalcanzable, `P964` Fair Code, `P965` marco-no-es-concesión); `Gap 335` (knowledge tracing) y
`Gap 356` descargados. **Detalle completo en el historial de git y en `*/trending.md`.**

### Mapa de oráculos — medido, y re-confirmado en el pase 93

`curl -sI https://github.com/<slug>` **no discrimina** bajo el proxy de egreso de estas sesiones: devuelve 403
para un slug real y uno inventado por igual. `api.github.com` igual. **Lo que sí discrimina:**
`git ls-remote --symref` (existencia, rama, SHA — un slug inventado falla con exit 128) y
`raw.githubusercontent.com/<slug>/<SHA>/<file>` (licencia; 🔴 **un 404 devuelve un cuerpo de 14 B, así que el
código HTTP se verifica siempre, no solo los bytes**). 🆕 **Positivo nuevo del pase 93: `WebFetch` sobre
`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` renderiza estrellas, forks y la licencia de la barra lateral** — de ahí
salen los ★ de este pase, 🔴 **y ahí se detectó que la barra lateral comparte el punto ciego de raíz del
escalador** (`P969`). Sigue vigente que `WebFetch` renderiza `github.com/topics/<t>`.
🔴 **Límite nuevo del sandbox: no se puede ejecutar código del repositorio**, de donde `P970`.

🆕 **Canal nuevo del pase 94 — la VERSIÓN de una plataforma (`P972`).** `git ls-remote --heads <slug>` y
`--tags <slug>` devuelven la escalera de releases que el proyecto mantiene de verdad, y el archivo de
versión del propio proyecto a un SHA fijado devuelve la cadena de release. 🔴 **Dos trampas medidas:**
`moodle/moodle` no tiene `version.php` en la raíz (está en `public/version.php` desde la 5.0 — `P973`), y
la escalera de `openedx/edx-platform` **se mudó de heads a tags y cambió de prefijo** entre Sumac y Teak
(`P977`), así que un sondeo de heads reporta una versión dos releases vieja **sin fallar**.
🔴 **El sandbox sigue sin ejecutar código del repositorio** (segundo pase), y
🔴 **`govinfo.gov`, `unesco.org` y `rdf.australiancurriculum.edu.au` se suman a los hosts bloqueados por el
allowlist de egreso: ya son ocho.** Per `P950`, no se reintentaron host por host.
